'Community spirit survives': The 100-year-old Halifax library rescued by volunteers which is now busier than ever

By Sarah Fitton
Published 7th Oct 2026, 09:24 BST

When Skircoat looked set to lose its local library, an army of determined volunteers stepped in to save the day.

Listen to audio version of this article

Now, as the building turns 100, it is again a team of dedicated people giving up their time who are keeping this community jewel not just open but thriving.

Skircoat Green Library, on Skircoat Green Road, was the first purpose-built public lending library to open in Halifax.

Its first borrower, back on September 30, 1926, was James Henry Whalley – one of the tenants of the John Mackintosh Memorial Homes.

It was run by Calderdale Council until it was named as one of several buildings the council was looking to hand over to community groups in 2020.

Dismayed by the prospect of losing their treasured library, residents teamed up to put together a case for the community asset transfer of the building.

That was approved in 2022 and by April 2024, the community had raised enough funds and done enough repair work to reopen the building as The Old Library.

Now it is a warm, welcoming haven for readers of all ages, especially those who enjoy a cuppa and a piece of cake.

Taking in around £20,000 a year, the addition of a cafe has provided a key income stream for the library, which also relies on donations and grants.

It hosts talks and children’s events, and has a host of regular borrowers who visit at least once a week.

The fact that it is open on a Sunday is particularly welcomed by many.

"We’ve had a huge amount of support,” said Sue Herbert, one of The Old Library’s trustees.

"No one in the area wanted to lose the library.”

There are around 6,000 books out on the shelves for people to borrow, including varied children’s and young adults’ sections.

Volunteer Michael Baim said some people come only to borrow books, some come to meet friends, others – particularly students – bring their laptops and use it as a work or study base.

For some people who live on their own, Sue said, it is a place where they can sit for free, keeping warm, whilst being around other people.

While the current arrangements are proving a huge hit, the library’s trustees have big plans for the future.

Underneath the space currently open to the public is a whole other floor – just as big in size – which they are hoping to put to good use.

They have already secured planning permission for an extension at the back of the building, allowing a dedicated staircase and lift to access the basement and ground floor to replace the current spiral staircase which is not suitable for public use.

The space downstairs could open up more potential uses for the library, such as a meeting place for community groups, more events and room hire opportunities.

The work will cost around £500,000 but the trustees are hopeful grants and fundraising will help them reach that total.

It is a 40-strong team of volunteers which keeps the library flourishing, spending their time checking out books, serving drinks, cataloguing books and helping maintain the library’s outside area.

One of the volunteers, who worked there when it was run by the council, explained what a hub it is for people who live in the area.

"Skircoat is a wonderful community,” she said. “When I worked in the library, I made many friends.

"Some people visited every opening day for the company so the library, even then, was more than a library.

"Two 90-year-old ladies used to meet up to reminisce about their time in Brownies together.

"I still see a lot of ‘my borrower friends’. We have a walking group who meet once a month and I’m still an active member of one of the many Skircoat Library readers groups.

"When I heard that a group of enthusiastic people had saved the library from permanent closure, I was delighted – the community spirit survives.”

The Old Library is in need of more volunteers – whether they can help only once a month or once a week.

People can also support the library by becoming a friend, donating £2 a month and being invited to help shape the future of the building.

For more information visit https://theoldlibraryskircoat.org.uk/

The Old Library is open from 10am until 4pm on Tuesdays, Thursdays, Saturdays and Sundays, and from 10am until 7pm on Wednesdays.
